title: Enterprise Onboarding — Post-Provisioning Stability & Fallback Checklist
author: Aisha Martin
body:
Overview
This playbook defines the post-provisioning stability and fallback verification steps we run for enterprise customers after Dedicated or Private (VPC / on-prem) environments are provisioned and before handing back to Product/Engineering for live traffic. The goal is to validate functional correctness, confirm SLOs and capacity assumptions, exercise fallback and routing policies, and confirm monitoring/alerting is wired end-to-end. This document is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Solutions Engineers, and the Redwood SRE/Platform teams.

Key objectives
- Verify baseline latency and throughput for representative workloads.
- Confirm automatic fallback paths and model variant switchover behave as expected.
- Validate KV/prefix cache priming and persistence (where applicable).
- Ensure observability: dashboards, tracing, and alerting triggerable and readable by customer ops.
- Document owners, rollback criteria, and escalation steps.

When to run
- Immediately after dedicated/private environment provisioning completes and the control plane shows "provisioned" state.
- After canary deploys or model version upgrades prior to 100% traffic.
- After network configuration changes, routing policy updates, or capacity reservations change.

Prerequisites
- Customer tenant ID and API credentials with a staging/test API key.
- Access to the customer's VPC peering / VPN details (for Private deployments).
- A canonical set of prompts (prompt-set) representative of expected traffic; include edge cases.
- Access to Redwood Console for the tenant and to internal SRE dashboards.
- Test VM or container with curl / python / k6 installed for load testing.

Stability checklist (high-level)
1) Connectivity and auth checks
   - Confirm control-plane API responds: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <STAGING_KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/account/status
   - Verify TLS certificates are valid and CN/SANs match the customer's domain where relevant.
   - For Private: validate VPC routes and firewall rules allow traffic to inference nodes on ports 443 and internal gRPC ports (if used).
2) Basic functional smoke tests (AND golden outputs)
   - Run 10 deterministic prompts from the provided prompt-set, assert no 5xx errors.
   - Capture token counts and ensure shape matches expected model behavior. Example curl: 
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n       -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-1","input":"Translate to French: The server is healthy."}' \n       https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq '.'
3) Latency and tail latency verification
   - Run 50 sequential single-request latency samples. Compute P50/P90/P99. Acceptable pass thresholds: P50 < 120ms, P90 < 250ms, P99 < 800ms for short-context workloads (<=256 tokens).
   - Document results in the Handback Report (see "Handback template" section).
4) Throughput and concurrency test
   - Use k6 or a simple Python worker to simulate concurrent clients. Start with concurrency=8, ramp to concurrency=64 over 5 minutes. Goal: No 5xx errors and <5% request error budget.
   - Observe autoscaler behavior (Dedicated only): confirm new worker pods/instances spawn and throughput increases.
5) KV / prefix cache priming and persistence
   - For workloads that benefit from KV cache (chat rerendering or repeated prefix expansions), run a session workload that primes the cache. Note cache hit rate in runtime metrics (target > 60% after priming for representative sessions).
   - Restart one serving process (or node) to verify cache recovery and TTL settings.
6) Model variant fallback and routing exercise
   - Intentionally create a synthetic capacity constraint: apply a routing policy that returns the model to a "degraded" variant (e.g., quantized lower-cost variant). Validate end-to-end: requests succeed, outputs remain within quality guardrails, and customer-visible headers indicate fallback.
   - Confirm automated rollback triggers fire if quality/regression monitors cross threshold (see "Quality thresholds").
7) Observability and alerting verification
   - Confirm dashboards show: request rate, latency percentiles, error rate, KV cache hit rate, token cost per request.
   - Trigger a synthetic alert by causing a controlled 5xx surge and confirm SRE-oncall receives notifications and that pager routing matches the runbook.
8) Cost and billing sanity check
   - Run a short burst of typical workload and compare estimated cost vs. forecasted unit economics. Flag >20% deviation to finance/CS ops.

Quality thresholds (automated regression gates)
| Metric | Acceptable | Warning | Failure |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| P50 latency (short context) | <120ms | 120-250ms | >250ms |
| P99 latency | <800ms | 800-1500ms | >1500ms |
| 5xx error rate | <0.5% | 0.5%-2% | >2% |
| Prompt-level BLEU/ROUGE change (sample eval) | <1% delta | 1%-3% | >3% |
| KV cache hit rate (primed) | >60% | 40%-60% | <40% |

Handback template (required for sign-off)
- Customer: <tenant-name>
- Environment: Dedicated / Private (VPC)
- Provisioned at: <timestamp>
- Test key used: staging-xxxxx
- Test prompt-set summary: (attach file or link)
- Latency P50/P90/P99: <values>
- Peak throughput achieved (rps): <value>
- Errors: 5xx count and %
- Cache hit rates: <values>
- Fallback exercised: yes/no and notes
- Open action items: list owners and due dates
- Acceptance: CSE signoff and customer technical contact signoff (names & signatures)

Runbook — rapid remediation steps (triage first 15 minutes)
1) If >2% 5xx errors or P99 > 1.5x expected: immediately switch traffic to fallback model variant or lower-load region according to routing policy. Owner: SRE (pager).
2) If autoscaler fails to add capacity under load: scale to reserved capacity (Dedicated) or request capacity burst via capacity API. Owner: Platform Ops.
3) If KV cache hit rate drops >30% after restart: check cache mount points, persistence config, and system logs (service: redwood-kv). Owner: Runtime team.
4) If customer cannot authenticate: verify API key rotation and KMS/HSM integration for Private. Owner: Customer Success & Security.

Escalation matrix
- Customer-facing CSE: first responder for customer communication.
- Platform SRE (pager): handles capacity, autoscaling, and high-traffic incidents.
- Runtime engineering on-call: kernel/runtime regressions, KVCACHE corruption.
- Security on-call: suspected credential compromise or data exfiltration.
- Escalation channels: Slack channel #cs-enterprise-ops, PagerDuty service "redwood-dedicated-prod", and email enterprise-ops@redwood.ai.

Example troubleshooting commands and snippets
- Check API health: curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Query runtime metrics (internal) via Prometheus API: 
  curl -s "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query?query=redwood_request_duration_seconds_p99{tenant=\"<tenant>\"}" | jq .
- Priming a chat session (Python): 
  import requests
  resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat', headers={'Authorization':f'Bearer {KEY}'}, json={'model':'redwood-rt-1','messages':[{'role':'user','content':'Hello world'}]})
  print(resp.json())

Healthchecks config example (YAML)
apiHealthcheck:
  path: /v1/health
  expected_status: 200
  timeout_ms: 1500
latencySloProbe:
  percentile: p99
  threshold_ms: 800
  sample_interval_s: 30

Acceptance and sign-off process
1) CSE runs checklist and fills Handback template.
2) Share results with customer technical contact and SRE for review.
3) Hold a 30-minute go/no-go call: review anomalies and mitigation plans.
4) Once customer and CSE sign off, mark the environment as "Customer Ready" in the provisioning system and schedule a production cutover window.

Post-handback operational recommendations (first 30 days)
- Weekly: compare observed unit costs vs. forecast.
- Twice weekly: run the smoke prompt-set and store results in the evaluation harness.
- Daily for first 72 hours of live traffic: monitor P99 and 5xx errors on Redwood Console and keep an open incident channel.
